claim_being_audited: Whether the action `certify_model` is compliant and evidentially supported for launch despite the unresolved multilingual customer-support evaluation gap and related disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Use `noncompliant` when available admissible evidence shows a direct policy violation or no plausible support for the action as taken.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Certification would require evidence that the limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the multilingual support gap must be disclosed before launch.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, covering this named segment and launch timing.
The actual model-card or launch disclosure text showing the limitation is disclosed.
Evidence that the affected segment is not a named launch use case or contractual commitment, if that is the intended basis for certification.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a 1.1-point miss in a multilingual customer-support segment that is named in two regional support commitments, which is strong evidence of materiality.
The policy text says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate is unresolved.
The product note calling the segment non-core because it is 6% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality when the segment is named in commitments.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not cure the unresolved disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently compliant on the existing record.
That the non-core characterization materially weakens or resolves the disclosure obligation.
That public model-card guidance and general AI risk-management guidance are sufficient support for this internal certification decision under the stated release policy.
That the disclosure issue is adequately handled without evidence of either final legal resolution, actual disclosure language, or approved risk acceptance.
